:: JUDGMENT:

The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the grievous injuries sustained by him, in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 07.12.2020 at about 14.45 pm., when the petitioner was pedestrian from his neighbor's house to his house near Thotadaguddadahalli village, Dasanapura Hobli, Bangalore and at that time, a Car bearing reg.No.KA-02-MM-7290 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.1856/2021 dashed against the petitioner so as to endanger human life.
Due to said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries to his left leg foot and injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was taken to Siddu Health Care Centre,
Nagasandra, Bangalore wherein he took first aid treatment.
Due to heavy pain on his left leg he was taken to Government Hospital, Holenarasipura, Hassan district as outpatient for a period from 14.12.2020 to 11.02.2021.
Petitioner has spent Rs.5 lakhs towards medical expenses.
The Madanayakanahalli police station, Bangalore have registered as case in crime No.547/2020 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.

Thereafter a charge sheet is filed against the driver of the vehicle under Section 279,
338 of IPC.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, due to the said accident he is unable to do his usual work as he was doing earlier and become permanently disabled.
The respondent No.1 is insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the vehicle involved in the accident
as on the date of accident therefore they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

Hence, he has prayed to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents.
3. The summons has been duly served on respondent No.1 and 2.

The Respondent No.2 has not Yashas S.T vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98549067/
2 appeared before this Tribunal.

sentences.text: Hence, Respondent No.2 has been placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared before this tribunal through his counsel and filed written statement.
He has denied the entire case of the petitioner as false and baseless.
However, he has denied that he issuance of policy in the name of M/s.Raj Trading Corporation in respect of the vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-02- MM-7290.
He has further contended that the driver of the car bearing reg.No.KA-02-MM-7290 is not having valid and effective driving licence to driver the said vehicle.
Further he has contended that the alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the Petitioner.
Hence, he SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.1856/2021 has prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 07-12- 2020 at about 14.45 p.m. when petitioner was pedestrian walking in a road, when he reached near Thotadaguddadahalli village, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru, at that time

the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MM-7290 drove in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, as a result of which petitioner sustained grievous injury, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so, from which respondent?
3.
What Order
or Award ?
5. The petitioner in order to prove her case her natural guardian/father has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9, Ex.P.13 to 24.
Senior Medical Officer has examined as PW-2 and got marked document as Ex.P.10.
Dr.Nagaraj.B.N. has examined as PW.3 and got marked documents as Ex.P.11 and 12.
On the other hand, the Legal Manager of Insurance SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.1856/2021 company has examined as RW.1 and no document has been marked through him.
6. Heard the arguments from both sides.
Perused the entire records.

7. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
REASONS 8. ISSUE No.1:- It is the case of the petitioner that on 07.12.2020 at about 14.45 pm., when he was pedestrian from his neighbor's house to his house near Thotadaguddadahalli village, Dasanapura Yashas S.T vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98549067/

sentences.text: Due to said accident, he sustained grievous injuries to his left leg foot and injuries all over the body.
On the other hand the Respondent No.1 has denied the entire case of the Petitioner as false and baseless.
SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.1856/2021 Therefore, the burden is on the Petitioner to show the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car in causing accident.
9. As already stated supra, the natural guardian/ father of the petitioner has examined himself as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to 9, Ex.P.13 to 24.
PW.1 has filed affidavit in lieu of his examination-in-chief.
He has reiterated the entire averments of the petition in his chief examination.
Ex.P.1 is the certified copy of complaint, Ex.P.2 is the certified copy of FIR, Ex.P.3 is the certified copy of charge sheet, Ex.P.15 is the rough sketch and Ex.P.24 is the Medial register document.

These documents reveals that the police registered FIR in Cr. No.0547/2020 with respect to the accident based on the complaint lodged by PW.1 against the driver of the offending Car bearing reg.No.KA-02-MM-7290 for the offences punishable U/Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.

Further it reveals that after due investigation, the police filed the charge sheet against driver of the offending Car bearing reg.No.KA-02-MM-7290 for the offences SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.1856/2021 punishable U/Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC.
10.
Ex.P.4 is the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner sustained left distal tibia fracture.
Except Ex.P.5 - OPD book, Petitioner has not produced discharge summary and also not produced any medical bills.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW.1 at length,
but he has failed to elicit anything from him to disbelieve his version.
It is relevant to note that PW.1 has categorically denied the suggestion that the petitioner was injured for his self- fall and not occurred accident as version of the complaint.
11. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not chosen to adduce any evidence in support of his contention.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to disbelieve that the charge sheet filed the police is collusive or defective.
The contents of the charge sheet reveal that the accident occurred only due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing reg.No.KA-02-MM-7290.

Therefore,
from the evidence of SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.1856/2021 PW1 and in the light of contents of charge sheet, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of offending Car.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in MV Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, based on the above discussion, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing reg.No.KA-02-MM-7290 is proved.
As such, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of discussion made while answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the minor petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the Yashas S.T vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98549067/
4 petitioner towards SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.1856/2021 medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during the treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
13.

sentences.text: The natural guardian/father of minor petitioner has contended that due to accident his son sustained grievous injuries.
In order to prove the injuries caused to him, he has produced Ex.P.4 wound certificate reveals that the petitioner sustained left distal tibia fracture.
In order to prove the same petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj, Senior Medical Officer, Holenarasipura through him got marked Ex.P.10 - MLC extract.
Petitioner has also examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P.11 - original calculation sheet and Ex.P.12 - X-ray.

He has deposed that, a patient by name Master Yashas aged 11 years came on 26.06.2022 for assessment of disability, he has given an alleged history of RTA on 07.12.2020 and sustained fracture of the left leg both bones distal third.
At the time of examination the petitioner complains of unable to walk fast or run and jump, unable to sit cross leg and squat.
On SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.1856/2021 examination, the petitioner has mild swelling of the left ankle and foot, restricted left ankle movements.
On recent X-ray of the left leg shows united fracture.

PW.3 has assessed physical disability of the left lower limbs at 30% and 10%
to the whole body.
14. It is relevant to note that age of petitioner is shown as 11 years as on the date of accident.
In this regard PW-1 has produced Ex.P.9 the copy of Aadhar card of petitioner.
As per this document the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 06.12.2010 and the accident took place on 07.12.2020.
Therefore, it is clear that as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 10 years.

15. At this juncture, it is relevant to refer the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 2445 between Master Mallikarjun V/s Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Ltd and another, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows:

If the disability is upto 10% to the whole body R s . 1 lakh, above 10% and upto 30%
to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs: upto 60%, Rs.4 lakhs, Upto 90% Rs.5 lakhs and SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.1856/2021 above 90% it should be Rs.6 lakhs.

For all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc.
16.
In the instant case also PW.3 has assessed 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head of pain and suffering already undergone including loss of amenities of life on account of disability.

17. Towards Medical Expenses :
As already stated supra, PW.1 has not produced discharge summary and has produced cash bills marked at Ex.P.6 which shows a sum of Rs.1,000/- was incurred towards the treatment of the petitioner.
Though the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW.1 but has failed to elicit any thing from him to disbelieve the medical bills.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for medical bills of Rs.1,000/-.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,000/- under the head Yashas S.T vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98549067/

sentences.text: 18. Towards Discomfort, inconvenience and loss SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.1856/2021 of earnings to the parents during the period of treatment:
It is relevant to note that the natural guardian of the Petitioner has not produced any document to show his avocation and income.
Even though natural guardian might have caused loss of some income and discomforts to the parents of the petitioner during the period of treatment.
Therefore, his parents are entitled for a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the heads of loss of income and discomforts to the parents.

19. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No.
1. loss of amenities of life on Rs. 1,00,000/-
account of disability 2.

Medical expenses Rs. 1,000/-
3. Discomfort, inconvenience and Rs. 40,000/-
loss of earning to the parents during the period of treatment Total Rs. 1,41,000 /-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,41,000/-.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

21. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the Owner of offending Car bearing reg.No.KA-02-MM-7290 and respondent No.1 is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 in the 'Partly affirmative'.
